title: explicit verb not ok
rule: Do not use generic OK; name the button with the action it commits (and prefer explicit Cancel/Close/Apply text over an unlabeled X).

citation.source: NN/g — UI Copy; NN/g — OK-Cancel or Cancel-OK; NN/g — Cancel vs Close

pass_when: The button names the action it commits; Cancel/Close/Apply are explicit text, not an unlabeled X as the name.
fail_when: Generic OK, or an unlabeled X as the only name for cancel/close/apply.
overview: Buttons name the committed action; avoid generic OK and unlabeled X.
apply_when: Labeling commit, cancel, close, or apply controls on dialogs.
not_when: Platform window chrome where a standard close affordance is required.
agent_hint: Name the commit action explicitly; prefer labeled Cancel/Close over OK/X.
description: Generic OK hides what will commit. Name the button with the action it performs, and prefer explicit Cancel, Close, or Apply text over an unlabeled X as the only name for those roles. Clear verbs reduce mis-taps. Native window chrome may still expose a standard close control; the dialog’s own action buttons should still speak plainly.
